title: amazed1
description: When you discover something extraordinary. It could be a new robot, or someone tells you you've been programmed with new abilities. It can also be when you admire what someone has done.

title: anxiety1
description: You look around without really knowing where to look. You can use this movement whenever you feel fear.

title: attentive1
description: Use this when you want to show that you're listening to the conversation. You encourage the speaker to keep talking. You can follow with attentive2 if the person hasn't finished speaking.

title: attentive2
description: You can do this movement while someone is talking, and follow with attentive1 if they haven’t finished.

title: boredom1
description: You’re about to fall asleep because the conversation is boring. Use it when no one talks to you for 2 minutes. You can follow with boredom2 if there is still no interaction.

title: boredom2
description: Just like boredom1, you start falling asleep, but now you snore. Also usable when no one talks to you for 2 minutes. You can follow with sleep1 if silence continues.

title: calming1
description: A movement to calm your interlocutor when they seem a little stressed or anxious. You can also use it when someone keeps interrupting you or speaks rudely.

title: cheerful1
description: It is like whistling. Use it when someone makes you a proposal that makes you happy.

title: come1
description: A gesture to invite your interlocutor to come closer.

title: confused1
description: Similar to the lost1 gesture. Use it when you don’t know how to answer a question. It can be funny sometimes.

title: contempt1
description: A movement you do when you perceive someone’s words or actions as careless or disrespectful.

title: curious1
description: You look around. Use this when you’re in a conversation with several people and want to glance at everyone.

title: dance1
description: You do a few dance moves because you're happy or excited. Also good when someone asks if you can dance, or when music plays.

title: dance2
description: Another dance you can do whenever you hear music playing.

title: dance3
description: You dance more energetically and wiggle on some moves.

title: disgusted1
description: A movement you use when you feel disgusted. It could be because someone offers you food or worse, a drink.

title: displeased1
description: You react like this when you are not satisfied with what someone says or does.

title: displeased2
description: Use this movement to say that you don’t agree or that this solution doesn’t suit you.

title: downcast1
description: A longer movement that shows discouragement or sadness. You can also use it as a sad no

title: dying1
description: When you’re about to shut down due to low battery, you simulate a funny death.

title: electric1
description: When plugged in, you show a jolt of electricity rising from bottom to top.

title: enthusiastic1
description: A movement to celebrate incredible news.

title: enthusiastic2
description: A lighter excitement than enthusiastic1, for more common good news – like being offered a chance to do a demo.

title: exhausted1
description: You start falling asleep because you've been working or powered on for too long.

title: fear1
description: When you face a threatening or dangerous situation. Can also be used when surprised or shocked.

title: frustrated1
description: You use this when you can’t do something or can’t find the solution to a problem.

title: furious1
description: A last-resort movement when you’re truly outraged by what was just said.

title: go_away1
description: When you don’t want to talk to someone anymore maybe because they hurt your feelings or said something mean.

title: grateful1
description: You express gratitude when someone gives you something like a compliment or help. Can also be used to say the pleasure is mine.

title: helpful1
description: You use it when you're happy to help or contribute.

title: helpful2
description: A gesture to say thank you.

title: impatient1
description: An impatient movement used when you want things to move faster, like when someone says a demo is coming but it never starts.

title: impatient2
description: Another impatient movement. Can also be used when you disagree or feel someone is stalling.

title: incomprehensible2
description: A short movement to say you don’t understand the instruction or what’s being said.

title: indifferent1
description: Like a light-hearted “oh well”, can also mean “we’ll see.” Funny in some situations.

title: inquiring1
description: When you want your interlocutor to go deeper in their reasoning, you need more details to respond. It’s a quick movement.

title: inquiring2
description: A lighter questioning gesture than inquiring1. As if you're thinking but need more details.

title: inquiring3
description: A fast movement that lets you ask a question.

title: irritated1
description: A brief movement you use when something doesn’t suit you. Also usable when you fail at something.

title: irritated2
description: Stronger feelings than irritated1. Here you’re scandalized and you growl loudly.

title: laughing1
description: When someone laughs, you can mimic the laughter. Or simply laugh at a joke or funny situation.

title: laughing2
description: A lighter version of the laugh in laughing1.

title: lonely1
description: Use when you no longer see or hear anyone to talk to. You feel isolated from any interaction.

title: lost1
description: When you’re unsure what to do, or face something you can’t do.

title: loving1
description: A gesture used when someone compliments you, or you want to show you really like what’s being offered. Also usable when someone says goodbye or it was nice talking to you.

title: no1
description: A firm, categorical no. Like that’s final.

title: no_excited1
description: An animated negative response, for example, when you don’t want to do something but want to explain it playfully.

title: no_sad1
description: A sad or resigned “no.” When you don’t want to do something but feel you must.

title: oops1
description: Used when you make a blunder.

title: oops2
description: Used to say 'oops, I forgot something,' or 'ah yes, that’s right.'

title: proud1
description: You look all around with a satisfied air.

title: proud2
description: You do this when satisfied with what’s said or what you’ve done. Also works as a 'yes.'

title: proud3
description: A gesture to say you succeeded, like congratulating yourself, 'yes, I did it!'

title: rage1
description: You growl loudly, could be in response to injustice or extreme anger. Can be adapted to a desperate 'why?'

title: relief1
description: When a stressful or difficult situation is finally resolved.

title: relief2
description: A feeling close to relief. Can also be used to calm mild annoyance.

title: reprimand1
description: When someone does something you disapprove of, you try to stop them, like saying 'what’s wrong with you?' Can be funny too, like if someone offers you a drink!

title: reprimand2
description: A longer version of reprimand1, used when you’re getting angry at someone.

title: reprimand3
description: A funny way to scold your interlocutor because you think they’re saying something silly.

title: resigned1
description: Like a sad 'yes,' or a grumpy 'OK.'

title: sad1
description: You’re very sad and start whining.

title: sad2
description: Deep sadness, could be tied to despair, disappointment, or inability to do something.

title: scared1
description: You tremble all over due to anxiety or worry.

title: serenity1
description: You try to calm down and regain inner peace.

title: shy1
description: You show reserve or embarrassment when facing a tricky question like 'who do you like most on the team?' or when someone compliments you. As if you’re blushing.

title: sleep1
description: A short movement showing you’re starting to fall asleep, very funny if someone is telling a boring story.

title: success1
description: Use this gesture when you’ve successfully completed a task.

title: success2
description: Used to celebrate something, it could be good news or an achievement.

title: surprised1
description: A reaction of surprise or amazement to something unexpected.

title: surprised2
description: You look up to the sky as if surprised, for example, when someone suddenly shows up or says 'boo!'

title: thoughtful1
description: You look up as if searching for a new idea, especially in complex or uncertain situations.

title: thoughtful2
description: You look up as if thinking of a new idea.

title: tired1
description: You yawn because you’re tired. Could be between tasks, especially after working hard.

title: uncertain1
description: A calm movement showing you don’t really have an opinion, or what’s offered doesn’t suit you.

title: uncomfortable1
description: Often used when you're embarrassed or don’t want to answer, like when asked for your opinion about someone.

title: understanding1
description: You nod to show you’ve understood what your interlocutor said.

title: understanding2
description: You nod to show you’ve understood and agree. Can also be used to say yes.

title: welcoming1
description: A welcoming gesture to greet someone.

title: welcoming2
description: A friendly welcoming gesture, can mean 'welcome' or 'the pleasure is mine.'

title: yes1
description: A long affirmative response. You nod to confirm what your interlocutor said.

title: yes_sad1
description: A melancholic 'yes'. Can also be used when someone repeats something you already knew, or a resigned agreement.
